copy attacks, main menu, a GK.Memory watch on +0x79 of the MainMenu/MM_Accept timeline's eoc::TimelineDataComponent: 0 -> 2 when the key on the 'press any key' page was pressed (writer bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x1D55BD7, from ecl::TimelineSystem's update) and 2 -> 0 9.6 s later (writer bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x1D522A3, called from bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x1D408B1 under SystemUpdate<ecl::TimelineSystem>); the camera of that timeline stopped moving in the same 0.27 s; the menu's looping timeline MM_Open_Boats holds 2 while playing

the fork F5 reads it per client tick for every TimelineData entity (TimelinePlayback rows): the five main-menu timelines (TimelineType 10) appear 0 at LoadMenu+0.8 s, MM_Open and MM_Open_Boats go 0->2 0.1 s later, MM_Accept and MM_Accept_Temple 0->2 155 ms after the splash key and MM_Accept 2->0 9.57 s after (three times: two starts and a return to the menu, which replays MM_Open too)

dx11 pseudo-code of the two writers the watch hit, both under ecl::TimelineSystem's update: bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x1D55400 stores 2 into the component's PlaybackState as it starts a timeline, and bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x1D51B40 stores 0 into the byte +0x79 of the component in its ending branch

survey.names: Every name here is Script Extender's author's (his headers), not the game's own: they are kept because they are what the extender's Lua answers to and what bg3_verify compares, and every field carries the rung `extender` - the extender's name for the field at that offset, which nobody has checked against the game's code. A name is raised from `extender` only with evidence from the code, by `gatekit names set`.
